referendum_required_for: revision of the constitution (approved by referendum, as in 1989)

government.note: Islamic republic under the Guardianship of the Islamic Jurist. The Supreme Leader is chosen, supervised and can be dismissed by the elected Assembly of Experts (88 members), and holds final authority over the armed forces, judiciary, state broadcasting, the Guardian Council and the Expediency Discernment Council. The directly elected President heads the government; the office of Prime Minister was abolished in 1989. The Guardian Council vets all candidates for the presidency, the Majlis and the Assembly of Experts before they may stand. The Assembly of Experts is not modelled as a legislative chamber (the schema has no slot for it); its elections are listed in elections.json. The Constitute Project describes the President as the de jure head of state in diplomatic functions, but the Supreme Leader is treated here as head of state and effective executive.

holders.vacant_reason: Office vacant after the death of Ali Khamenei. Under Article 111 of the constitution an Interim Leadership Council of the President, the Chief Justice and a Guardian Council jurist exercised the Leader's duties from 1 to 8 March 2026, until the Assembly of Experts named a successor.

system.note: Single- and multi-member constituencies; an absolute (later qualified) majority wins in the first round, otherwise a plurality runoff. All candidates are vetted by the Guardian Council. 270 seats on 1 January 2000 (5th Majlis, elected March/April 1996); enlarged to 290 from the February 2000 election (6th Majlis met in May 2000). seats_2000 uses the last election before 2000 (1996), as summarised by Nohlen et al. (2001), who count independents as allies of the three blocs.

chambers.review_note: Bloc seat counts for the 5th Majlis differ by source: Nohlen et al. give CCA and allies 110, Combatant Clerics and allies 80, Executives of Construction and allies 80 (used here, with the five minority seats folded into the blocs); Adelkhah gives Right 90-100, Executives of Construction 70-80, Left about 40; Kazemzadeh gives hardliners 150, Rafsanjani/Executives of Construction 15-60, Imam's Line 30, independents 30. Confirm a preferred breakdown. Also confirm whether the Majlis should count as a confidence chamber (it votes confidence in individual ministers).

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Estimate, not a measured distribution: candidate vetting limits what national votes can show. Anchored on the 1997 presidential election (Khatami, reformist, 69.07%; Nategh-Nouri, CCA, 24.91%; other candidates about 6%) and the 1996 Majlis blocs. Reformist support is split between the Islamic-democrat camp; principlist support between velayat-e faqih conservatives (shia_theocratic) and other religious conservatives (islamist). Small shares are assigned to currents that could not appear on the ballot (secular liberals, monarchists, the secular left) and to ethnic-regional movements; these are gameplay estimates.
